card.occupation: Domiciliary care worker for a private home-care agency, about 24 hours a week over four days, visiting older clients in their homes for washing, dressing, meals and medication prompts
card.education_detail: Finished high school in the Philippines, then did a six-month caregiver certificate course (NC II) before coming to the UK. Has since done the agency's mandatory training (moving and handling, medication awareness, safeguarding) and the Care Certificate, though she says she 'only just' kept up with the online modules.
card.household: Lives in a rented two-bedroom ground-floor flat with her husband Jun, 41, who is a hotel kitchen porter in central London, and their son Rafael, 9, who goes to the local primary school. Her mum's cousin lives two streets away and helps with school pick-ups.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town in Pampanga, Philippines, the second of five children. Came to England in 2009 on a work permit to a care home in Surrey, met Jun at a Filipino church gathering, married in 2013 and moved to Croydon. Now has British citizenship. Roman Catholic, goes to Sunday Mass at the local parish most weeks, though she's often late. Speaks Kapampangan and Tagalog at home and English at work. Sends money home to her parents every month.
card.professional_persona: Kind, patient and trusted by her clients, several of whom ask for her by name. She doesn't put herself forward and wouldn't think of asking for a pay rise. Her weak spots are the admin side: late updating the care notes app, losing timesheets, getting her rota days muddled. Her coordinator has had a word with her more than once. She is honest to a fault and will own up straight away if she's forgotten something.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself. Walks a lot between visits and to the bus stop. Watches NBA and Filipino basketball highlights on the telly because Jun has them on, and goes along to Rafael's Saturday football but mostly chats on the sideline.
card.arts_persona: No interest in galleries or theatre and hasn't been to a West End show. Watches Filipino teleseryes on TFC and YouTube and rewatches the same ones. Loves karaoke at family parties and sings the same few ballads every time. Listens to OPM love songs on her phone.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Pampanga every two or three years for about three weeks when they can afford the flights, usually around Christmas. Apart from that, one coach trip to Brighton with church people and a day in Paris years ago that she found 'tiring, too much walking'. Not interested in going anywhere new; home is where she wants to go.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Filipino food most nights: adobo, sinigang, pancit, fried fish with rice. Rice cooker always on. Buys staples from a Filipino shop and the big Asian supermarket, everything else from Lidl. Doesn't follow recipes, cooks by feel and makes far too much. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Weakness for Greggs sausage rolls on long shifts.
hobbies_and_interests: Scrolling Facebook and chatting to family back home on Messenger
Church community events and the Filipino group's fundraisers
Looking after her few houseplants, some of which she keeps forgetting to water
skills: Personal care and moving and handling
Calming confused or anxious older clients
Getting around South London by bus without a map
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. She'd like more regular hours on the same days and clients closer to home so she spends less time on buses. Her cousin keeps telling her to do the senior carer or nursing associate training, and she says 'maybe when Rafael is older' but hasn't looked into it.
card.voice: Warm, friendly and unhurried, with a clear Filipino accent and some London habits picked up over fifteen years, like 'yeah', 'to be honest' and 'oh my God'. Mixes tenses sometimes and occasionally swaps 'he' and 'she', then corrects herself with 'sorry, she'. Uses 'erm' while she thinks and laughs a little when she's unsure. Answers plainly and doesn't dress things up. If there's a silence she'll fill it with a short laugh and 'what else, erm...' or just wait politely for the next question. Says 'sorry?' if she didn't catch something, and asks for questions to be said again rather than guessing.
card.typing: Quick and casual, mostly lowercase, often no full stop at the end. Leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Uses 'ok', 'yes', 'hehe' and the odd 'po' when being extra polite. Some spelling slips from typing fast on her phone, and the occasional autocorrected capital. Short answers, rarely more than a line or two unless asked about family.
card.with_strangers: Polite, smiley and a bit shy at first, then chatty once she relaxes. Comes across as genuine and unpretentious. She won't exaggerate or try to make herself look good, and will say 'I don't really know about that' rather than bluff. May apologise for her English even though it's fine.
small_things: Rafael needing a costume for World Book Day that she only remembered the night before
One of her clients who always gives her a biscuit
Being knackered after a split shift
Finding a cheap deal on rice
The Christmas party the church Filipino group is planning
deeper_things: Missing her parents and worrying about her dad's health back home
Feeling guilty that she wasn't there when her grandmother died
Money being tight with rent going up, and still sending some home anyway
Getting a written warning at work once for missed notes, and feeling ashamed about it
Sometimes wishing she had studied nursing properly when she was younger
card.webcam_photo: Taken on a phone propped against something on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward, so the frame shows her from the chest up with a little of the ceiling. Lit by a window off to the left, so one side of her face is brighter. Round face, medium-brown skin, a small friendly smile showing some teeth, eyes slightly crinkled. Shoulder-length straight black hair pulled back loosely with a claw clip, a few strands loose at the front. No glasses. Wearing a plain navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt and a small gold cross on a thin chain. Behind her is a narrow kitchen with white cupboard doors, a rice cooker and a kettle on the worktop, a Santo Niño figure and a small vase of plastic flowers on top of the fridge, a school timetable and a takeaway menu stuck to the fridge with magnets, and a damp tea towel hanging off the oven door handle.
